_doc: THE ENGRAVING RULES — LGMF PLAN 2e (planned 2026-09-27, RUNNING_LOG §408 … §447; built from §448). Every placement and style rule of the notation lives HERE, in five tables, each row with its `basis` (lilypond · gould · composer §N · AI §N · census) and its `ref` (the § or the day that decided it). The devices and the look blocks of container.json POINT at these rows ("@objects.cueHead.size"); notation/lib/rules.js compiles the pointers into the registry keys the layout and the renderer read, and throws on a pointer with no row. docs/ENGRAVING_RULES.md is GENERATED from this file (tools/gen_engraving_rules.js) — never hand-edit it. tools/check_rules.js holds the gates. THE FIVE LAYERS (§413, his 'yes'): (1) THE ANCHOR — which point of a unit sits on x(t) · (2) THE COLUMN — the order and the side of what stacks on a unit · (3) THE OBJECTS — one row per drawn object type, four distances in ss (`parent` to what it hangs on · `staff` the floor from the staff edge · `stack` to the next stacked mark · `beside` horizontal) + face · size · colour · (4) THE PAGE — page_rules.json `edge` (not here: one table per file) · (5) THE EXCEPTIONS — the ladder. A value marked `census` is what drew on 2026-09-27 when the tables were built (2e.1, a re-housing: every page byte-identical); a later decision changes the ROW, with its §, and the page follows.

principles._doc: THE PRINCIPLES (PLAN 2l, 2026-09-28 — RUNNING_LOG §513 … §522): what a class of marks is FOR, before its numbers. A row's numbers serve its principle; a principle changes only at his word, with its §.

curves.rule: THE PERFORMER PRINCIPLE (A): a performer reads a curve in real time at the page's px/s, against the cursor and the tube; the curve is the shape with the best chance of the sound he composed, not a true picture of the mathematics. THE SCALE (C): eight names, ppp … fff, the performer's discrete resolution; continuous change is a curve between two of them; the height between two names must be visible. THE INTENTION IN SHAPES (F): a volume change is compositional intention in a few shapes — the swell, the rise and its mirror, the brief smooth dip, the brief smooth peak; read the data into the shape, draw the shape. THE DISCRIMINATOR: SHAPE-FIRST (hand-drawn — the sound followed the shape: #5's trills, #2's tremolos) is kept as drawn; FADER-FIRST (a generator's ride — the sequence's, the morph's, the texture's) is redrawn from its recipe. AT THE CURSOR MOTION AND NAMES, AHEAD THE SHAPE: a device at the cursor gives a motion cue or a reading in the performer's units; a device ahead gives a shape; a height without a scale gives neither.

objects._doc: LAYER 3 — THE OBJECTS (§421 · §422 · §427 · §428): one row per drawn object type. FOUR DISTANCES in ss — `parent` to what it hangs on · `staff` the floor from the staff edge · `stack` to the next stacked mark · `beside` horizontal — and a FIFTH (2h.1, §474, his 2g.6 eye): `after`, the horizontal clearance a time-spanning object keeps between its END and the leftmost ink of the next unit. `face` · `size` (ss for text, a scale for a glyph) · `colour` (a key of `colours`). `draws` names the layout's item kinds this row covers (`kind` or `glyph:<name pattern>` or `anim:<kind>` or `kind[seq]`) — gate (2): a drawn kind with no row fails the build. `variantOf` marks a row that draws with another row's glyph at its own size. His approved numbers are kept; anything undecided is seeded from LilyPond 2.24.4's define-grobs.scm on his machine (§422) — a seed is marked basis lilypond. New sizes are chosen on LilyPond's step 2^(1/6) (§428). `in` names where a value that is not compiled still lives (glyphs.json standards, a code literal) — the census of §448. 'leaves' (§458, his (a)): the order a mark leaves the head side when the ladder flips — 1 the ANNOTATION (the words and the symbols; the default for a row without the field), 2 the PITCH DATA (the cents and the partial), which stays with the head until nothing else helps.

accidental.courtesyNote: §500 (2026-09-28, his word at the running order's step 7 — 'a'): THE ACCIDENTAL POLICY ACROSS TIME. NO courtesy natural on a later plain head of the same letter and octave in the same voice, whatever the distance in time. The ONE exception is `naturalInColumn` — two heads sounding AT ONCE in one chord column, same letter and octave, one altered (2h.7, §479). Written as a row so the question is not decided twice

pitchPicture._doc: THE PITCH PICTURE OF A JUST NOTE (docs/research/just_partials_notation.md §1a, REVISED 2026-09-27): the accidental shows the NEAREST point on the quarter-tone grid — |cents| < edgeCents → the plain accidental of the tempered spelling · ≥ edgeCents → a quarter-tone sign; no arrows (the six arrowed glyphs stay baked in glyphs.json, unused). THE SPELLING: the origin is the nearest tempered pitch (|cents| ≤ 50); a quarter-tone sign points from the origin toward the truth, so a sharp-side deviation is spelled with a natural or a sharp (½♯ · ¾♯) and a flat-side one with a natural or a flat (the reversed flat · ¾♭): D♯ +41 is D¾♯ +41, D♯ −41 is E¾♭ −41, never E¼♭ / D¼♯. The picture is taken in the realization's WRITTEN pitch; the cents and the partial never change with it.

A morph is NOT a new section (LG-117, his: 'the sequence seamlessly moves into this'): its word is the sequence's, so nothing is written at a morph's entry. vibMarks._doc: THE VIBRAPHONE'S MARKS IN A SEQUENCE (PLAN 2g — §463 · §465 · §466; LG-116, his: 'hairpins describe dynamic movement and direction. The dynamic markings describe a relative level'): notation/lib/vib_marks.js reads each bow's slice of its seat's level curve into names and TIMED hairpins, tied to the BOW. The level = sequence_overlays.js writtenAt (the body through the part's ladder × the fade weight, §462 · §465) in written steps (0 ppp … 7 fff, −1 niente). A LEG (a monotone run between the turning points, the flats ignored) of ≥ hairpinSteps draws a hairpin; of nameSteps … hairpinSteps only when its rounded end name differs from the current name; under flatSteps nothing. A name at a leg's end where the rounded level differs from the current name, at the time reached (a plateau's start). No name without a hairpin, no hairpin without motion. `carry`: a bow's start name is its chain's previous bow's END name, never re-rounded — re-read from the level only at the chain's first bow and after a rest of ≥ restS. A bow whose fade rises from 0 opens with the niente circle in place of its start name; the fade-out ends at the level reached (the circle at 0). `repeatName` false: a flat bow at the carried level draws nothing. `flip` false: a voice's row is meaning — the ladder never flips these marks. minHairpinSs: a hairpin shorter than this between its marks is dropped, the names stand. The voice of a bow: `voice`.

And then extend the hairpins'): THE ○ STANDS WHERE THE FALL ENDS — a bow whose fall closes on the niente circle (the level under ppp rounds to nothing) while the row's next bows, abutting and bare, keep falling: ONE hairpin runs THROUGH those bows and the ○ stands at the end of the last. The marks carry through · endEvent; the layout ends them on the LAST bow's bar
vibMarks.crossBackNote: §678 (2026-10-01, his decision after §676's count — 'let's switch them back. So each side represents one voice. And let's use B … the top, the go line on the left side, and bottom go line on the right side'): THE ROWS ARE THE TWO VOICES AGAIN — crossAtUnison false: a chain keeps its row (navy top · olive bottom) for its whole sequence, each row ONE dynamic flow; §496's cross (crossNote, kept as the record) withdrawn — it changed hands at 4 unisons and restated 18 names. crossedLead 'opposite': at a CROSSED UNISON (the two rows' bows begin within crossS and the top row's head stands crossSteps staff steps or more UNDER the bottom row's — 7 in Draft 01: 42.65 · 72.32 · 120.74 · 818.95 · 824.41 · 856.17 · 862.37) the top row's lead rises on its head's LEFT edge and the bottom row's falls on its head's RIGHT edge, so the two dotted lines never lie on each other; everywhere else both leads stay on the left edge
vibMarks.crossNote: §496 (2026-09-28, his word — 'it is one player 2 bows'): the two rows are the player's two BOWS, not two people, so the notation may assign them for legibility. At a RHYTHMIC UNISON (both chains begin within crossS) whose heads stand a clear top and bottom (crossSteps staff steps apart or more — the chord column displaces a second) the rows CROSS: the higher note takes the top row (navy) from there, the lower the bottom (olive), and both rows begin their story again (a restart: the start name written). A side-by-side pair (a unison or a second) keeps the rows as they were. His words: 'when there's a unison, rhythmic unison, and there's clearly a top and bottom … let's allow a cross there. So the top note goes with the top, the blue, and the bottom note goes with the green … but only in these cases'. Draft 01: 11 rhythmic unisons, 9 with a clear top and bottom, 7 of them crossing; the colours of the bar, the lead and the swatch follow the ROW
vibMarks.rowsNote: 2i.1, §487 — his decision §485 (B): the two rows are the two SEATS — chain 0 the TOP row (navy) and chain 1 the BOTTOM (olive) for the whole sequence, whatever the pitches do; chain 0 is the top when its first bow of the sequence sounds at or above chain 1's first, else the bottom (a tie → chain 0 top). 2g's rows by REGISTER (§464 his (A), the value `register`) are superseded: at a crossing two bows shared a row (23 of 156 in Draft 01) and a name was restated at every switch (44)

And the hairpin adjusted accordingly': the bow's LAST mark (a name or ○ reached) is right-justified to the bar's end (after 2h.1's cut) when, centred on its time, it would run past it; its hairpin's end follows; a name reached earlier in the bow stays at its point (Gould) — the AI's reading of 'at the end of a bow', CONFIRMED at his word 2026-09-28, the running order's step 6, §499: a name reached mid-bow keeps telling its time; only one that would hang past the bar's end slides back to it
